Jackline, Determined To Succeed
The story of Jackline Wambui Muthoni, a form two student at
Kahuhia Girls in Murang’a is one of remarkable determination
and hard work. Bright eyed and full of promise, Jackline wants to
be a doctor because she is so fascinated by surgical procedures,
but the nobler reason she confesses is because she wants to help
people and change their lives by enhancing their health. Her
journey began right from primary when she was just a young
girl in a boarding school. She would wake up very early to study,
which is quite an unusual feat for a primary school going child
to delve into, voluntarily. “I would wake up in the morning at
2a.m. and read even up to 4a.m. then go back to sleep till five
in the morning,” she divulges. Her reason: “Being honest I was
a noisemaker”, she admits her eyes dancing with mischief, “but I
would make up for the lost time. “During the day, our break was 30
minutes. I would go take tea for 10 minutes, the next 20 minutes I
would try and study together with my best friend Tabitha.
I would also try to concentrate during preps,” she reveals.
However, even Jackline had no idea that her commitment to
her studies would reward her in days to come. Today she is
receiving a Cheque of Ksh. 185,000 from Crown Berger Ltd, the
paint manufacturer to pay for her school fees. On joining Kahuhia
Girls School, her mother’s main challenge was raising money to
pay her school fees. Thank God her mother who is HIV+ was in
constant contact with KENWA (Kenya Network of Women with
Aids), where she receives counseling and post HIV/AID testing for
opportunistic infections and control through adherence to drugs
and certain nutritious foods. She decided to approach them for
support. KENWA whose mission is to improve the quality of lives
of Women living with HIV/AIDS and their children as well, agreed
to support her. They have a strict policy that for a student to be
even considered for sponsorship they have to excel in academic
performance. They found that in Jackline- her grades at the school
were excellent and she was a promising student.
This is despite the fact that when she joined Kahuhia Girls she had
a mean grade of B-, she got 348 marks. Though she did not meet
her goal thus missing Limuru Girls by a whisker, she held on to
her resolve to be an A-student regardless of where she ends up.
Needless to say that when she finally reported to Gandu Girls later
than her peers she managed to work very hard to catch up. Her
grades at the school speak for themselves, as she has managed to
maintain an A-streak.
So when KENWA went around scouting for donors to sponsor her,
they found Crown Berger who were at the same time looking for
an opportunity to sponsor a disadvantaged child. They were told
about Jackline. She continues studying at Kahuhia Girls blowing
